Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Zakariel usually hope their child will grow to embody god remembered and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: זכריאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: זכריאל הוא שם שמקורו בעברית ומורכב משני חלקים: 'זכר' שפירושו 'אלוהים זכר' ו-'אל' שפירושו 'אלוהים'. השם מופיע בתנ"ך ופירושו 'אלוהים זכר את החסד שלו' או 'אלוהים זכר את עמו'. השם נמצא בספר נחמיה 12:36 ו-זכריה 1:1, וגם שם של כוהן ששימש בתקופת נחמיה.

in_greek.name: Ζαχαρίας
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός μνήμη τοῦ ἐλέους αὐτοῦ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ζαχαρίας εἰς τὸ ὄνομα ἀπὸ τῆς Ἑβραϊκῆς γλώσσης, συνεσταμένον ἐκ τῶν λέξεων 'זכר' καὶ 'אל', ᾧ σημαίνει 'Θεός μνήμη τοῦ ἐλέους αὐτοῦ' ἤ 'Θεός μνήμη τοῦ λαοῦ αὐτοῦ'. Τὸ ὄνομα ἐμφανίζεται εἰς τὴν Καινήν Διαθήκην καὶ δηλώνει τὴν μνήμη τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐπὶ τῆς εὐσπλαχνίας αὐτοῦ.

in_latin.name: Zachariiel
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Zachariiel derivatur ex hebraeo 'זכריאל', compositum ex 'זכר' quod significat 'Deus recordatus est' et 'אל' quod est 'Deus'. Nomen hoc in Biblia Hebraica invenitur et significat 'Deus recordatus est misericordiam suam' vel 'Deus recordatus est populi sui'. Nomen etiam in Ecclesia primitiva adhibitum est.

in_english.name: Zakariel
in_english.meaning: God remembered His mercy or God remembered His people
in_english.long_meaning: The name Zakariel originates from Hebrew 'זכריאל', a combination of 'זכר' (zakhar) meaning 'to remember' and 'אל' (El) meaning 'God'. It appears in the Bible, specifically in Nehemiah 12:36 and Zechariah 1:1, signifying 'God remembered His mercy' or 'God remembered His people'. Historically, the name has been used in Jewish and Christian traditions, symbolizing divine remembrance and mercy. The name conveys spiritual significance, suggesting a connection to God's benevolence and remembrance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Zakariel carries impressive cultural roots as it originates from the Hebrew language, which is rich in history and significance for the Jewish and Christian faiths. It's the name of an ancient biblical figure, Zacharias, who played an essential role in the progression of God's plan in history, by being the father of John the Baptist. The name Zakariel passes down the heritage and traditions of the Hebrew culture in an impactful way, offering a sense of continuity, spiritual strength, and connection to the past.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Zakariel signifies 'God remembered.' This carrying a profound reminder that, no matter how difficult life may be or how overlooked one feels, God never forgets His children. The name serves as a daily motivation to remember that even in adversity, God's promises remain steadfast and unfaltering, inspiring the bearer to stay the course of faith and trust in God's infinite love and care. Additionally, the significance of the name 'Zakariel' highlights the importance of personal memory and reflection – to recall God's faithfulness and grace throughout history, and to remember the sacrifices and actions of God's faithful servants who went before.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The name Zakariel means "God remembers" or "God of remembrance," highlighting the importance of God's unfailing memory and commitment to His people.

biblical_reference.note: The name appears in the Hebrew Bible and is associated with a priest during Nehemiah's time and the prophet Zechariah.

historical_references.reference: In Jewish mythology, Zakariel is the name of an angel believed to be in charge of memory and recollection. This is a reference to the biblical figure Zadkiel, who is mentioned in the Book of Enoch as one of the seven archangels and the leader of the fourth heavenly domain.

In Christian tradition, Saint Zakarie (Zachary) is the name given to a priest in the New Testament who was visited by the angel Gabriel to announce the birth of John the Baptist. This is a continuation of the Jewish tradition, as Zachary is also mentioned in the Old Testament and is the same figure as Zadkiel in Jewish mythology.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Christian name 'Zakariel' has seen a modern resurgence in various contexts, particularly in New Age spirituality, fantasy literature, and role-playing games. In New Age spirituality, Zakariel is sometimes adopted as a personal Name of God or as the name of an angelic being. In fantasy literature, Zakariel is the name of a character in various books and series, such as the 'Wheel of Time' by Robert Jordan or the 'Anathem' by Neal Stephenson. In role-playing games, Zakariel is a popular name for characters, especially in Dungeons & Dragons, where it is sometimes associated with archangels or guardian figures. Overall, the name Zakariel has taken on a more mystical and spiritual significance in modern culture, often used to evoke images of power, protection, and otherworldly beings.
